name: rogue-legacy-a
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE production illustrated-science-fiction game-art atlas for Frontlines. Square 2048x2048 artwork with EXACTLY FOUR equal square full-bleed paintings in a precise 2-by-2 grid, no gutters, no margins, no frames, no captions, no text or numbers. Each painting stays inside its quadrant; do not blend scenes across the two midlines. Polished detailed painted graphic-novel military concept art, matching worn armor and cinematic lighting of a serious military strategy game. NOT a photograph, NOT flat vector art, NOT anime. Coherent equipment, convincing anatomy, controlled lighting, readable silhouettes. Center each primary face/helmet AND distinctive equipment/action in the central 70 percent of its tile; readable at card thumbnail size. Four intentionally different compositions, camera angles and tactical subjects. No excessive bloom, logos, badges or UI.
ROGUE: patched olive and tan armor, scavenged asymmetrical but functional equipment, mint-green equipment lights, field repairs and improvised weapons, reclaimed industrial terrain, practical determined soldiers.
TOP LEFT: A patched portable field workshop fills the scene: mismatched welded bench, reclaimed power cells, practical hand tools and a partially repaired armored component. A small mechanic in the background supplies scale.
TOP RIGHT: A resourceful field soldier helps a wounded ally back behind a scrap-built rear barricade, carrying their damaged weapon and kit. Visible wounds in armor remain; this is a costly tactical withdrawal, not rejuvenation.
BOTTOM LEFT: A fatigued scavenger soldier refastens a loose armor strap, collects their modified rifle and rises to move again. An improvised practical adjustment restores readiness amid a rough battlefield.
BOTTOM RIGHT: A patched-armored skirmisher breaks contact through a jagged side alley while incoming rounds strike discarded scrap cover behind them. Readable retreat direction and evasive movement, without teleportation.
